title: Machame Route on Kilimanjaro: Day-by-Day Guide
excerpt: The Machame Route is the most popular way up Kilimanjaro. Here is what each day looks like, how hard it is and who it suits.
body:
The Machame Route is the busiest route on Kilimanjaro, and there is a good reason for that. It is scenic, it has a natural rhythm of climbing high and sleeping lower, and it fits in six or seven days. Its nickname, the "Whiskey Route", comes from its reputation as the tougher alternative to the Marangu "Coca-Cola" route.

## How the route runs

Machame starts on the southern slope, at Machame Gate (about 1,800 m). You walk through rainforest on day one, out onto heather and moorland on day two, and then across the Shira Plateau towards the Lava Tower. From there the route drops into the Barranco Valley, climbs the famous Barranco Wall, traverses to Karanga and Barafu camps and finishes with a night ascent to Uhuru Peak at 5,895 m.

## Day by day on the 7-day version

1. **Machame Gate to Machame Camp** – forest trail, five to six hours.
2. **To Shira Cave Camp** – steeper, out of the trees, views open up.
3. **Via Lava Tower to Barranco Camp** – you climb to around 4,600 m and sleep around 3,900 m. This is the key acclimatisation day.
4. **Barranco Wall to Karanga Camp** – a scramble with hands, not technical, and great fun for most people.
5. **To Barafu Camp** – a short day to rest before the summit.
6. **Summit night and descent** – start around midnight, reach Uhuru Peak after sunrise, descend to Mweka or Millennium Camp.
7. **Down to Mweka Gate** – through the forest again, certificates at the gate.

## Six or seven days?

We almost always suggest seven. The extra day at Karanga is not wasted time: it gives your body one more night to adapt before the summit push, and that is what decides most climbs.

## Who Machame suits

Machame suits fit walkers who like variety and do not mind sharing campsites. It is busier than Lemosho or Rongai, especially in January, February and from July to October. If you want quieter trails with the same scenery, look at the [Lemosho Route](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/), which joins Machame on day three.

## What our partner takes care of

Our local partner Kilimanjaro Nature Tours runs every climb with licensed mountain guides, a cook and porters, and checks oxygen saturation twice a day. You can see a sample programme on our [Machame itinerary](/itineraries/machame-route-7-days/) and read more on our [Kilimanjaro page](/climbing-kilimanjaro/).
